[RT-1] Unbounded SSE stream holds heavy LLM work
File: src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: The route opens a long-lived ReadableStream and calls generateDocsWithStreaming which runs multiple ChatOpenAI streaming workflows; the handler never checks request.abort/request.signal or cancels work on client disconnect. Impact: With many concurrent clients this will exhaust serverless/instance capacity and OpenAI API quotas (wasted CPU and cost), causing dropped throughput and failed requests. Fix: Stop work on client disconnect (use request.signal), enforce per-client concurrency/queueing, and move heavy LLM generation to a background job (queue + polling/webhook) with a short-lived streaming proxy.

Impact: Multiple concurrent streams cause API rate-limit exhaustion, high latency, and eventual system-wide failures under moderate client load. Fix: Add global and per-user rate limits, a bounded worker pool/queue for LLM calls, and apply circuit-breaker / retry policies to prevent cascading overload.

[RT-2] No backpressure or concurrency control for per-request LLM fan-out
File: actions/context.ts (L1-L250)
Evidence: generateDocsWithStreaming and the streaming helpers launch serial/parallel multi-step LLM streams (PRD→PLAN→phases→nth-phase) for each request with no rate limiting, concurrency caps, or slow-client handling. --- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-3] Public SSE endpoint with no auth or throttling
File: src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: The route returns text/event-stream with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' and performs no authentication/authorization before starting expensive generation. Impact: Open endpoint can be abused to trigger many LLM jobs, quickly consuming API quota and compute resources. Fix: Require authenticated requests, enforce quotas/rate-limits, and add request size/complexity checks before scheduling generation.

[RT-4] Streaming doesn't detect or handle client-side slow reads
File: src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: controller.enqueue is used without handling backpressure/queue-full or catching failures from slow consumers; no chunk-size or batching strategy is implemented. Impact: Slow clients can cause memory growth / stalled server tasks or dropped updates if internal queueing fails under bursty updates. Fix: Monitor controller.desiredSize / batch updates, throttle send rate, and implement time-based flushing or drop policy for non-critical interim updates.

--- INFO ---

[RT-5] Collaboration packages present but no sync provider implemented
File: package.json and src/components/tiptap/rich-text-editor.tsx
Evidence: Dependencies include yjs / y-protocols and Tiptap collaboration extensions, but editor components do not import or initialize a Yjs provider or any server relay.
